O pagamento das faturas processar-se-á nas condições legais e regulamentares que disciplinam o processamento, liquidação e pagamento de despesas pelo contraente público. 2. Os acertos do número de páginas efetivamente produzidas pelos equipamentos serão efetuados semestralmente após apresentação de relatórios de consumo, tendo por base os valores constantes da proposta e a diferença entre o volume de páginas contratado e o volume de páginas produzido. 3. Section I: Program Overview & Background 1.1 Purpose The Department of the Air Force (DAF), Business and Enterprise Systems (BES) Directorate, AFLCMC/GBGD, is issuing this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) to identify and acquire an innovative, commercially available Digital Adoption Platform (DAP). This platform will replace the legacy Oracle User Productivity Kit (UPK), which is reaching its official end-of-life. The primary goal of this acquisition is to secure a modern, sustainable, enterprise-ready so

User Productivity Kit (UPK), which is reaching its official end-of-life. The primary goal of this acquisition is to secure a modern, sustainable, enterprise-ready software-guided training and performance-support tool. It must streamline content creation, simplify software adoption, and provide real-time in-application guidance for the DEAMS user base. 1.2 Mission Impact & Capability Gap The current solution (Oracle UPK) represents unsupported software and significant technical debt. Its retirement creates a critical operational gap in how training is conducted across the enterprise. The replacement DAP will modernize training material outputs, provide interactive in-application assistance, and reduce the overall training footprint. This capability is designated as a Criticality (1) — Must Have requirement to support continuous financial and enterprise operations. 1.3 Scope of the Target Environment • User Base: Approximately 26,000+ geographically dispersed personnel across 170+ global locations. • Primary Integration: Stable and proven integration with Oracle e-Business Suite (EBS) (including F orms & OAF pages) and modern web applications. • Target Environments: The DAP must be deployable and tested across both Development (Dev) and Test environments before transitioning to

Addendum to RFO 52.212-2 – Evaluation Procedures and Criteria for Selecting Proposals GBG will utilize a two-step evaluation process. In step 1, Oﬀerors submit a cover letter, ROM, white papers and an eligibility checklist. In step 2, Oﬀerors will submit a proposal and present a live pitch virtually or in-person to the GBG team. After receipt of step 1 proposals, the Air Force will conduct an evaluation based on three factors: technical, importance to agency programs, and funds availability. • The technical factor will assess how innovative the solution is (as deﬁned in this announcement) and the feasibility of the solution solving the unit’s challenges. • The importance to agency programs factor will assess the solution’s potential to enhance the mission eﬀectiveness of the unit. • The funds availability factor will assess the availability of funding to purchase the solution at Pitch Day. Price shall be considered to the extent appropriate, but at a minimum, to determine that the price is fair and reasonable. As such, ensure that the total price is included in your proposal. designed so that under all conditions specified herein (installation, deinstallation, transportation, operation, and maintenance) and under all likely fault conditions (including human error), it protects against the risk of electric shock and other hazards. All hazards shall be eliminated or reduced to the lowest risk level practical using methods in the following order of precedence: design; incorporation of safety devices; incorporation of warning devices; technical manual procedures; and New Equipment Training (NET) and sustainment training. Catastrophic and critical hazards (as defined in MIL-STD-882) shall not rely solely on warnings, cautions, or procedures/training for control of risk. Electrical Safety Electrical materials and equipment shall be selected, applied, installed and protected in accordance with NFPA 70. Where COTS equipment is used, the contractor shall select equipment that has been listed or certified by a Nationally Recognized Test Laboratory such as UL. The listing or certification shall cover the intended equipment usage and operating environment. Operators shall not be exposed to components with voltages exceeding 30 volts (V). thout explicit Government approval. Exposed and under-floor wires and cables in the EEB shall be of the low smoke zero halogen (LSZH) type. This requirement is not applicable to the internal wiring of equipment racks, LRIs and DLRIs. Additional Safety Provisions Audible and visual warning devices shall be provided to indicate malfunctions and hazardous conditions that could cause injury and/or equipment damage. Audible warning signals shall be distinguishable from other sounds under normal operating conditions. Visual signals shall be readily visible and easily recognized. The current legacy analog infrastructure limits scalability, resilience, and interoperability. Under this Call for Solutions, the selected vendor will deliver, integrate, install, and acceptance-test a flexible, open-standard, modular Digital IF solution across up to twenty (20) worldwide satellite communications (SATCOM) teleport sites. Increment 1 will establish a fully operational baseline designed to support subsequent capability upgrades and integrations in future fiscal years. SECTION 2 – REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION PROBLEM STATEMENT Area of Interest: Modular Digital Intermediate Frequency Solu

quires an open-standard Digital IF architecture. However, before committing to a full-scale global deployment, the DoW must validate the operation, interoperability, security, and performance of these modular commercial solutions in a rigorous representative environment. Technical Objective & Scope The DoW seeks a commercial solution for an Increment 1 Digital IF capability set built on a flexible, open standard (e.g., Digital Intermediate Frequency Interoperability compliant), modular architecture. The selected solution will undergo standard site acceptance testing and operational verification to confirm compliance with contract performance requirements and site compatibility. Upon successful acceptance, this operational configuration will serve as the standardized baseline for deployment and installation across up to twenty (20) worldwide SATCOM teleport sites. Mission Impact Successful validation and deployment of this flexible open-standard Digital IF architecture will directly enhance warfighter lethality and survivability by delivering a highly resilient, agile, and survivable GEO-SATCOM capability which rapidly adapts to contested/congested environments. The current legacy analog infrastructure limits scalability, resilience, and interoperability. Under this Call for Solutions, the selected vendor will deliver, integrate, install, and acceptance-test a flexible, open-standard, modular Digital IF solution across up to twenty (20) worldwide satellite communications (SATCOM) teleport sites. Increment 1 will establish a fully operational baseline designed to support subsequent capability upgrades and integrations in future fiscal years. SECTION 2 – REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION PROBLEM STATEMENT Area of Interest: Modular Digital Intermediate Frequency Solu

quires an open-standard Digital IF architecture. However, before committing to a full-scale global deployment, the DoW must validate the operation, interoperability, security, and performance of these modular commercial solutions in a rigorous representative environment. Technical Objective & Scope The DoW seeks a commercial solution for an Increment 1 Digital IF capability set built on a flexible, open standard (e.g., Digital Intermediate Frequency Interoperability compliant), modular architecture. The selected solution will undergo standard site acceptance testing and operational verification to confirm compliance with contract performance requirements and site compatibility. Upon successful acceptance, this operational configuration will serve as the standardized baseline for deployment and installation across up to twenty (20) worldwide SATCOM teleport sites. Mission Impact Successful validation and deployment of this flexible open-standard Digital IF architecture will directly enhance warfighter lethality and survivability by delivering a highly resilient, agile, and survivable GEO-SATCOM capability which rapidly adapts to contested/congested environments. The current legacy analog infrastructure limits scalability, resilience, and interoperability. Under this Call for Solutions, the selected vendor will deliver, integrate, install, and acceptance-test a flexible, open-standard, modular Digital IF solution across up to twenty (20) worldwide satellite communications (SATCOM) teleport sites. Increment 1 will establish a fully operational baseline designed to support subsequent capability upgrades and integrations in future fiscal years. SECTION 2 – REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION PROBLEM STATEMENT Area of Interest: Modular Digital Intermediate Frequency Solu

quires an open-standard Digital IF architecture. However, before committing to a full-scale global deployment, the DoW must validate the operation, interoperability, security, and performance of these modular commercial solutions in a rigorous representative environment. Technical Objective & Scope The DoW seeks a commercial solution for an Increment 1 Digital IF capability set built on a flexible, open standard (e.g., Digital Intermediate Frequency Interoperability compliant), modular architecture. The selected solution will undergo standard site acceptance testing and operational verification to confirm compliance with contract performance requirements and site compatibility. Upon successful acceptance, this operational configuration will serve as the standardized baseline for deployment and installation across up to twenty (20) worldwide SATCOM teleport sites. Mission Impact Successful validation and deployment of this flexible open-standard Digital IF architecture will directly enhance warfighter lethality and survivability by delivering a highly resilient, agile, and survivable GEO-SATCOM capability which rapidly adapts to contested/congested environments.
